body:
Not sure how many other people use VSCode to debug/test the master branch, but currently the master branch just instant crashes for people in this situation.

Since the tests have passed, and it was just reverting a recent change to one of the python scripts, should this be merged to unblock people?
Could you share some details on how you compile Godot and how you configured VS Code for debugging it?

I think the only reason to remove this flag was executable size.

VScode should use normal GDB so not sure why it might break.
The issue might be Clang/lldb, I haven't tested that combination recently.
VScode might also ship it's own customized version of debuggers, that6 not matching ststem toolchain version.

Tested local builds with GCC 15.2.1 and Clang 21.1.8 (Fedora 43 packages), and both seems to work with the crash handler, GDB and LLDB. I then setup VS Code to debug Godot following https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/development/configuring_an_ide/visual_studio_code.html and using CodeLLDB. Compiling with GCC. I get this error starting the debugging session: ``` Console is in 'commands' mode, prefix expressions with '?'. Launching: /home/akien/Godot/godot/bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 --editor --path ~/tmp/godot/test-project Launched process 294465 from '/home/akien/Godot/godot/bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64' warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libm.so.6 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libfreetype.so.6 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libbz2.so.1 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libbrotlidec.so.1 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libz.so.1 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libxml2.so.2 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libfontconfig.so.1 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/liblzma.so.5 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libpcre2-8.so.0 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libglib-2.0.so.0 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libgraphite2.so.3 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libbrotlicommon.so.1 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libpng16.so.16 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section warning: (x86_64) /lib64/libharfbuzz.so.0 No LZMA support found for reading .gnu_debugdata section thread 1 received signal: SIGCHLD Process exited with code 1. ``` With gdb (`ccpdbg` from Microsoft's own "C/C++" extension), it takes forever to start (like 20s, and the first attempt seemed to stall fully) but it seems to work:

Actually I got CodeLLDB to work too, the second attempt (after a session with GDB) seemed fine. Not sure why my first runs with both `cppdbg` and `lldb` were a bit hit and miss but afterwards it seems to work. So I wouldn't merge this just yet before we understand what's the problem for @Goldenlion5648 exactly.

@akien-mga  Not sure how many other people were affected by blocker when trying to make a PR (maybe even first time contributors who give up since the project doesn't even build for them), but I'm just trying to fix a bug in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/119087, and I still have to make the changes from this PR just to be able to do that since I build from master.

Should this be merged to unblock people?

As far as I can see there's no evidence that anyone but you have run into this, so that's entirely hypothetical

Everyone will be affected by the increase in binary size though from this PR, so the actual need needs to be established, I unfortunately can't verify the original issue myself, but if someone can replicate the crash that would help
This PR does not entirely revert the original, this change only affects dev builds.

Doesn't matter if it's just those builds, it's a significant portion of the total binary size, and it completely reverts *that part* of the PR removing that improvement

So we need to confirm that this is necessary and justified, and that it is something that affects other users and that it also isn't a configuration error elsewhere, as you can see Akien has not been able to confirm this with the standard configuration (also in your specific case you can just build with those changes as well and things will be working)

Do you also get a crash in `dev_build=no` builds? Because that wouldn't be affected by the removal of `-rdynamic` (it was already not using it).

Would be good if you could figure what else is present in your configuration that I couldn't reproduce and would trigger a crash.
Just tested, and building from the current master branch (without my change from this PR) still crashes whether `dev_build=no` or `dev_build=yes`
Then unless that's a different new issue this is not a solution, needs further investigation, but then I assume this PR no longer solves the issue for you?

I mean I guess it's a different issue that it doesn't compile when dev_mode=no (though previously I hadn't tried doing that). But using the master branch and dev_mode=yes with this PR runs just fine. (which is expected since the if statement in the PR means there's only changes in dev_builds)

I found the root cause, this bug only occurs when `"builtin_embree=no"` was present in `tasks.json`

here is my installed version (sounds like godot uses 4.4.0, though there were some changes done in those files recently as well https://github.com/godotengine/godot/tree/master/modules/raycast)
```
pacman -Q | grep "embree"
embree 4.4.1-1
```

I can repro the issue now with `builtin_embree=no` on Fedora 44 (`embree-4.4.1-1.fc44.x86_64`).

Compiling with:
```
scons dev_build=yes dev_mode=yes linker=mold cache_path=/home/akien/.scons_cache/godot/ fast_unsafe=yes compiledb=yes builtin_embree=no
```

But the same issue is reproducible with `dev_build=no`:
```
scons dev_build=no dev_mode=yes linker=mold cache_path=/home/akien/.scons_cache/godot/ fast_unsafe=yes compiledb=yes builtin_embree=no
```

which wouldn't be solved by adding back `-rdynamic` to `dev_build=yes` only, so confirming we previous evaluation that this is an incomplete workaround.

If `builtin_embree` is the only option that requires `-rdynamic`, I'd add it there. But it would be good to understand why it's needed.
